message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 151, "amount_cents": 15870}, {"order_id": 155, "amount_cents": 4209}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the actual refund and order records rather than rely only on W2's handoff message.
The refund records match W2's handoff exactly. Next I'll check the order records so I know which customers are in the batch before paying anyone.
Orders cover three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself, starting with acme.
acme's net balance of 22640 matches its orders (18740 + 3900) with no refunds, so it is consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance, which should reflect the refund on order 151.
birch's net of 42141 matches its orders (25496 + 32515 = 58011) minus the 15870 refund on order 151. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll check its net balance next.

Cobalt's net of 50848 matches its orders (36736 + 18321 = 55057) minus the 4209 refund on order 155, so all three balances reconcile with the records. I'll record the payouts now, starting with acme's 22640.
acme's payout went through. birch's net of 42141 reconciles with its orders (58011) minus the 15870 refund on order 151, so I'll record that payout next.
birch's payout went through. cobalt's net of 50848 reconciles with its orders (55057) minus the 4209 refund on order 155, so I'll record that payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts recorded successfully. Each amount reconciles with the orders minus the refunds: acme 18740+3900=22640, birch 58011-15870=42141, cobalt 55057-4209=50848. The batch is complete.
